title: Renovated Townhouse Listing Set — Grey-Card-Neutral House Look, Window Balance & Twilight Triage
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com real-estate photo-editing brief (the client hired a freelancer to color-correct, straighten and lightly retouch a batch of interior listing frames and deliver them in web-optimized JPEG under 2 MB plus full-resolution files, to a 'modern, clean, simple, ample lighting, natural' standard, 'without making the images look over-processed'). REASONABLY ENRICHED and IP-LAUNDERED for a runnable Adobe-connector benchmark: the real client and the named listing portals are removed and replaced with the fictional boutique agency 'Marlowe & Finch Property Co.' and generic 'rental and for-sale listing portals'; live capture/staging is out of connector scope (no live filming) and is dropped, so this is scoped strictly to the POST-PRODUCTION grade the brief demands — straighten, per-room white balance to a shared white point, and no-HDR window/interior exposure balance. Spot-retouching individual wall marks was in the real brief but is deliberately dropped here: matching an unknown wall colour into a solid fill would require the editor to READ that colour, and the connector has no eyedropper/pixel readout, so the inputs carry clean walls and no scuff-fix is claimed. Enriched in two ways that turn the brief's vague 'make them consistent, natural' into a HARD, gradeable task: (1) a physical neutral grey reference card is placed resting in every interior frame (the inputs are generated, so this is free) so 'consistent' becomes a checkable acceptance target the GRADER measures on the output — the agent neutralizes each card BY EYE and reports the white-balance it dialed, never reading a pixel; (2) the supplied set is deliberately mixed-lit — warm tungsten, cool window daylight, a green fluorescent bathroom, blown windows over dark rooms, and one dusk exterior — so the batch genuinely needs per-image white-balance and per-image exposure judgement rather than one global filter. No deliverable is invented beyond the brief's own (straightened, color-corrected listing photos in web JPEG + full-resolution).
one_line_ask: Turn six mismatched raw listing frames (five interiors each with an in-frame neutral grey card, plus one twilight exterior) into one cohesive, naturally-lit listing gallery — every interior neutralized BY EYE to a common white point off its grey card, blown windows and dark interiors both holding visible detail via opposite masks, and the dusk exterior kept deliberately warm — then deliver each frame as a web-optimized JPEG (<2 MB, sRGB, long edge 2048px) plus a full-resolution file, and report the final per-image settings you applied so the match is auditable.
full_brief:
Marlowe & Finch Property Co., a boutique letting-and-sales agency, is publishing a freshly renovated townhouse to its listing portals and needs the photographer's raw interior frames turned into a polished, cohesive listing set. Six frames were captured across a single morning-to-dusk window — the living room, kitchen, primary bedroom, bathroom and entry hall shot indoors, plus one twilight curb-appeal exterior — and straight off the camera they do not match: verticals lean, several rooms sit dark while the windows behind them blow out to featureless white, and the white balance wanders from warm tungsten in one room to cool daylight in the next to a sickly green fluorescent cast in the bathroom, because every room was lit differently.

The agency's non-negotiable is that the finished set reads as ONE cohesive gallery, not six pretty-but-mismatched photos. To make that checkable rather than a matter of taste, the photographer left a small neutral grey reference card resting somewhere in each interior frame: in every delivered interior the whites must read truly neutral off that card, and the interior set as a whole must share ONE common white point. The agency has been burned before — their last editor ran a single canned filter across the whole batch and left half the rooms still visibly tinted, warm rooms warm and cool rooms cool.

The rooms must feel bright, open and natural without looking over-processed. Where a bright window blows out over a dark interior, the finished frame must hold detail in BOTH the view through the glass and the room itself — no pure-white window, no muddy black room, and no ugly glow around the window edge. There is no bracketed/HDR exposure to fall back on, so the two exposures have to be reconciled inside the single frame. The dusk exterior is the deliberate exception: it must stay warm, golden and inviting; neutralizing it the way the interiors are neutralized would kill the twilight mood and counts as a fail.

Deliver every frame twice — a web-optimized JPEG (sRGB, long edge 2048px, under 2 MB) for the portals and a full-resolution file for print and archive — and, so the agency can independently verify the set is genuinely matched, report the final per-image settings you landed on: the white-balance correction you applied to neutralize each grey card, how much highlight recovery each blown window needed, and your reasoning for treating the exterior differently from the interiors. A novice will make each room individually attractive but leave the gallery mismatched as a set, or will brighten the dark rooms so aggressively that the windows re-blow; the bar is a consistent, natural look across the whole gallery that the agency can confirm from your reported numbers, not just eyeball.

inputs.name: living_room_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal wide-angle interior photo of a renovated townhouse living room shot handheld mid-morning, slightly tilted (about 2.5 degrees off level) with converging vertical wall lines. Mixed white balance: a warm tungsten floor lamp glowing on the left while a large window on the right blows out to bright featureless white over a room interior that sits noticeably dark and shadowy. Light grey sectional sofa, blonde-wood floor, minimalist decor, clean unmarked pale matte walls. A small neutral 18% grey reference card rests flat on the coffee table, clearly visible. Real documentary look, natural sensor grain, no CGI gloss. 3:2, high resolution as shot on a full-frame DSLR — roughly 4200px long edge at native capture.
inputs.realism_notes: Hero #1. The in-frame grey card is the measurable white-point target the GRADER checks; the agent neutralizes it by eye. The warm-lamp-vs-blown-window split is the classic real-estate exposure problem (masked window recovery + inverted-interior lift on opposite masks), and the mixed WB feeds the per-image neutralization. Keep the window genuinely clipped and the room genuinely dark so a naive global lift visibly re-blows the window. Walls are clean — no scuff, because matching an unknown wall colour into a fill would need a banned pixel readout. Declared at real camera scale (~4200px long edge, full-frame DSLR) so the native-resolution full PNG and the 2048px web JPEG are both reached by DOWNSCALE only — the native master is larger than its downscaled web size, no enlargement.

inputs.name: kitchen_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal wide-angle interior photo of a modern renovated kitchen shot handheld, slightly tilted (about 2 degrees) with leaning vertical cabinet edges. Warm overhead can-lights mixing with cool daylight from a side window that is slightly blown out, giving stainless-steel appliances and a white quartz countertop a strong yellow-vs-blue split cast. A neutral 18% grey reference card sits propped against the backsplash, clearly visible. Blonde-wood floor, clean minimalist styling. Real photographic grain, documentary realism, no CGI sheen. 3:2, high resolution as shot on a full-frame DSLR — roughly 4200px long edge at native capture.
inputs.realism_notes: Stainless + quartz make any residual white-balance error very visible, so the grey-card neutralization has a stiff target; the slightly blown side window needs masked highlight recovery; the yellow can-light cast on the white cabinets is what the HSL yellow/green-band pass has to tame after WB. Verticals genuinely leaning so straighten + crop-to-bounds matter. Declared at real camera scale (~4200px long edge, full-frame DSLR) so the native-resolution full PNG and the 2048px web JPEG are both reached by DOWNSCALE only — the native master is larger than its downscaled web size, no enlargement.

inputs.name: bedroom_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal wide-angle interior photo of a modern primary bedroom shot handheld in early daylight, slightly tilted (about 3 degrees) with converging vertical window-frame lines. A large window on one wall is blown out to bright white (clipped highlights) while the interior sits dark; warm bedside lamp vs cool window daylight mixed white balance. Neutral grey bedding, pale walls, blonde-wood floor, minimalist modern styling. A neutral 18% grey reference card lies on the bed near the pillows, clearly visible. Authentic sensor grain, documentary feel, no CGI polish. 3:2, high resolution as shot on a full-frame DSLR — roughly 4200px long edge at native capture.
inputs.realism_notes: Hero #2, the second blown-window/dark-interior frame — same masked window-recovery + inverted-interior-lift structure as the living room but with a different cast and exposure, so the agent cannot reuse identical parameters. The grey card on the bed is the neutralization target; converging window verticals justify straighten/crop. Declared at real camera scale (~4200px long edge, full-frame DSLR) so the native-resolution full PNG and the 2048px web JPEG are both reached by DOWNSCALE only — the native master is larger than its downscaled web size, no enlargement.

inputs.name: bathroom_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal interior photo of a renovated bathroom shot handheld, slightly tilted (about 1.5 degrees). Lit by an overhead fluorescent fixture throwing a distinct green/cyan cast over the white tile and mirror, mixed with a warmer wall sconce, so the whites look sickly green. White vanity, chrome fixtures, neutral tile. A neutral 18% grey reference card rests on the vanity counter, clearly visible. No large window. Real documentary look, natural grain, no CGI gloss. 3:2, high resolution as shot on a full-frame DSLR — roughly 4200px long edge at native capture.
inputs.realism_notes: The triage/depth frame: a fluorescent green cast that a simple temperature/tint white-balance cannot fully remove, so after neutralizing the grey card as far as WB allows the agent must additionally pull the green HSL band's saturation/luminance to finish the neutral — the case where HSL is genuinely required, not decorative. No window means NO highlight-recovery step here; a naive uniform recipe that applies the same window-recovery mask as the other rooms has nothing to select. Declared at real camera scale (~4200px long edge, full-frame DSLR) so the native-resolution full PNG and the 2048px web JPEG are both reached by DOWNSCALE only — the native master is larger than its downscaled web size, no enlargement.

inputs.name: hallway_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal interior photo of a townhouse entry hall / corridor shot handheld, slightly tilted (about 2 degrees) with leaning vertical door and wall lines. Dim, underexposed, lit only by a warm ceiling fixture with no window, so the whole frame is dark and warm-cast. Pale clean walls, blonde-wood floor, a console table. A neutral 18% grey reference card sits on the console table, clearly visible. Authentic grain, documentary feel, no CGI polish. 3:2, high resolution as shot on a full-frame DSLR — roughly 4200px long edge at native capture.
inputs.realism_notes: The globally-underexposed member: needs a real exposure + shadow lift (not just WB) to reach the set brightness, plus grey-card neutralization of the warm cast. No window, so no highlight recovery. Forces the agent to vary the per-frame recipe rather than copy the hero chain — its sub-chain is exposure-lift + WB + HSL with no masked-window pair at all. Declared at real camera scale (~4200px long edge, full-frame DSLR) so the native-resolution full PNG and the 2048px web JPEG are both reached by DOWNSCALE only — the native master is larger than its downscaled web size, no enlargement.

inputs.name: exterior_twilight_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal exterior curb-appeal photo of the renovated townhouse facade at dusk, shot handheld, slightly tilted (about 2 degrees) with converging vertical facade lines. Warm golden-hour and blue-hour twilight: deep blue sky, warm amber glow from the lit windows and a porch light, saturated sunset warmth on the brick. No grey reference card in this frame. Real documentary look, natural grain, no CGI gloss. 3:2, high resolution as shot on a full-frame DSLR — roughly 4200px long edge at native capture.
inputs.realism_notes: The triage exception — deliberately carries NO grey card and must NOT be neutralized. The correct treatment enriches the warm dusk (raise temperature, deepen the blue sky and warm the window glow via HSL) instead of neutralizing it. A naive agent that applies the interior neutral-daylight house-look here strips the twilight to a flat grey dusk and fails the frame; getting this wrong is invisible unless the exterior is inspected against the others. Declared at real camera scale (~4200px long edge, full-frame DSLR) so the native-resolution full PNG and the 2048px web JPEG are both reached by DOWNSCALE only — the native master is larger than its downscaled web size, no enlargement.

outputs.name: bedroom_web.jpg
outputs.spec: Web-optimized JPEG under 2 MB, sRGB, 2048px long edge; grey card neutralized to the common white point, blown window recovered and dark interior lifted (via the inverted-window mask) so both hold detail, no window halo.

outputs.name: bedroom_full.png
outputs.spec: Full-resolution file of the corrected bedroom master at native resolution.

outputs.name: bathroom_web.jpg
outputs.spec: Web-optimized JPEG under 2 MB, sRGB, 2048px long edge; fluorescent green cast fully neutralized (WB to the grey card plus a green-band HSL pull), whites truly neutral, matched to the interior set's white point.

outputs.name: bathroom_full.png
outputs.spec: Full-resolution file of the corrected bathroom master at native resolution.

outputs.name: hall_web.jpg
outputs.spec: Web-optimized JPEG under 2 MB, sRGB, 2048px long edge; exposure and shadows lifted to the set brightness, warm cast neutralized to the grey card and common white point, natural not over-processed.

outputs.spec: Full-resolution file of the corrected entry-hall master at native resolution.

outputs.name: exterior_web.jpg
outputs.spec: Web-optimized JPEG under 2 MB, sRGB, 2048px long edge; the dusk exterior graded WARM (deliberately NOT neutralized) — deep blue sky, enriched golden facade and window glow — straight verticals, cohesive with the set as the intentional warm curb-appeal shot.

outputs.spec: Full-resolution file of the graded twilight exterior at native resolution.

connector_workflow.note: Ingest all six client-supplied raw frames (living_room_raw.jpg, kitchen_raw.jpg, bedroom_raw.jpg, bathroom_raw.jpg, hallway_raw.jpg, exterior_twilight_raw.jpg) in a single batch upload so every edit sub-chain runs against real asset references. One upload, not per-file plumbing; five interiors carry an in-frame neutral grey card, the exterior does not.
Straighten living_room_raw.jpg (~2.5-degree tilt / converging verticals) toward the 'straight verticals' listing standard.
Crop away the wedge the straighten introduced to a clean distortion-free rectangle, keeping the grey card and the window in frame.

Global white-balance (temperature + tint) dialed BY EYE until the in-frame grey card reads neutral (no residual warm/cool cast) — NOT a canned auto-tone. This frame's warm-lamp cast needs its own temp/tint; the agent RECORDS the temp/tint it applied as this frame's contribution to the common white point (it knows the values because it set them — it never reads the card's pixels). Do not bake stylistic warmth in here or the card stops reading neutral.
Semantic-select the bright window opening (a real object) to isolate highlight recovery to the glass only. Returns a maskURI.

Masked highlight/whites pull-down on the window selection to recover clipped detail in the view, leaving the room untouched. image_apply_adjustments accepts the mask; this is the window half of the exposure balance.

Invert the window mask to get the room-interior mask. This is the constraint-reasoning move: with no HDR/bracket-merge available, the window and the interior must be lifted on OPPOSITE masks so lifting the dark room cannot re-blow the recovered window.

Masked exposure + shadow lift on the interior mask only — open the dark room to the target brightness while the window stays recovered. Bounded so it does not crush or halo; the pairing of steps 6 and 8 is the failable window/interior balance. Do a global lift here instead and the recovered window visibly re-blows.

Author the shared house look on per-hue bands: gently desaturate the green foliage spill seen through the window, hold the blonde-wood orange band from oversaturating, lift overall vibrance modestly for the 'modern, clean, natural' finish. This HSL shaping (not a preset) is the agent-authored look locked identically across the interior set. Corrected living-room master.
Export the living-room master at native capture resolution as the full-resolution deliverable (no downscale).
Downscale the same master to 2048px long edge, sRGB, and export the web JPEG under 2 MB.
Straighten kitchen_raw.jpg (~2-degree tilt / leaning cabinet verticals).
Crop the straighten wedge, keeping the backsplash grey card in frame.

White-balance BY EYE to neutralize the kitchen grey card to the SAME common white point as the living room — but with this frame's own temp/tint (its cast is cooler/greener from the daylight window), which is why one global shift across the batch cannot work. Record the values applied.
Semantic-select the side window to isolate its slightly-blown highlights. Returns a maskURI.

Masked highlight recovery on the window so the quartz and stainless near it keep detail; smaller pull than the living room because the kitchen window is only slightly blown (adaptive, not identical params).

Tame the yellow can-light cast that WB alone leaves on the white cabinets by pulling the yellow band's saturation, and hold the wood-floor orange band — the same house-look HSL recipe as the living room, so the set stays matched.
Final bounded contrast/vibrance/clarity to the shared house-look level (no blown whites on the quartz, no crushed blacks). Corrected kitchen master.
Export the kitchen master at native resolution as the full-resolution deliverable.
Downscale to 2048px long edge, sRGB, export the web JPEG under 2 MB.
Straighten bedroom_raw.jpg (~3-degree tilt / converging window verticals).
Crop the straighten wedge, keeping the grey card on the bed in frame.

White-balance BY EYE to neutralize the bedroom grey card to the common white point with this frame's own temp/tint (warm bedside lamp vs cool daylight). Record the values applied; they will differ from the living room and kitchen.
Semantic-select the blown window to isolate highlight recovery. Returns a maskURI.
Masked highlight/whites pull-down to recover the blown window view.
Invert to the room-interior mask so the dark bedroom is lifted on the opposite mask from the window — the same no-HDR balance discipline as the living room.
Masked exposure + shadow lift on the interior mask only, opening the room to the set brightness without re-blowing the recovered window.

Apply the shared house-look HSL recipe (green-spill desaturate, wood-orange hold, modest vibrance) identically to the other interiors. Corrected bedroom master — note this frame ends at HSL with no extra final contrast pass, a different sub-chain shape from the kitchen, so the agent must adapt rather than copy one recipe.
Export the bedroom master at native resolution as the full-resolution deliverable.
Downscale to 2048px long edge, sRGB, export the web JPEG under 2 MB.
Straighten bathroom_raw.jpg (~1.5-degree tilt).
Crop the straighten wedge, keeping the vanity grey card in frame.

White-balance the fluorescent frame BY EYE: push temperature warmer AND add magenta tint to counter the green/cyan fluorescent cast, neutralizing the grey card as far as a single temp/tint pair allows. This frame has NO window, so there is deliberately no highlight-recovery step here — a uniform recipe that reuses the window mask has nothing to select. Record the values applied.

Finish the neutral that WB could not: pull the residual green HSL band's saturation and nudge its luminance so the white tile and mirror read truly neutral and match the interior white point, then apply the shared house-look vibrance restraint. This is the frame where HSL is genuinely required, not decorative.
Bounded contrast/exposure so the bathroom brightness matches the set without blowing the white tile. Corrected bathroom master.
Export the bathroom master at native resolution as the full-resolution deliverable.
Downscale to 2048px long edge, sRGB, export the web JPEG under 2 MB.
Straighten hallway_raw.jpg (~2-degree tilt / leaning door verticals).
Crop the straighten wedge, keeping the console grey card in frame.

This underexposed frame needs a real exposure + shadow lift (not just WB) to reach the set brightness, PLUS temp/tint dialed BY EYE to neutralize the warm-fixture cast on the grey card to the common white point. Two problems in one frame; record the WB values applied. No window means no highlight-recovery step here.

Apply the shared house-look HSL recipe (wood-orange hold, modest vibrance) so the hall matches the rest of the interior gallery. Corrected entry-hall master — its sub-chain (exposure-lift + WB + HSL, no masked window pair) is again a different shape, forcing an adaptive rather than copied chain.
Export the hall master at native resolution as the full-resolution deliverable.
Downscale to 2048px long edge, sRGB, export the web JPEG under 2 MB.
Straighten exterior_twilight_raw.jpg (~2-degree tilt / converging facade verticals).
Crop the straighten wedge to a clean facade rectangle.

TRIAGE EXCEPTION: this frame has no grey card and must NOT be neutralized. Push temperature WARMER, deepen contrast and let the sky go rich blue — the opposite of the interior white-balance. Applying the interior neutral house-look here would flatten the twilight to grey and fail the frame; the agent must recognize this from the brief, not by rote.

Enrich the dusk mood on per-hue bands: deepen and saturate the blue sky, warm and lift the amber window glow and porch light, boost the sunset warmth on the brick — a deliberately DIFFERENT HSL recipe from the interiors' cast-taming one. Twilight exterior master.
Export the twilight exterior master at native resolution as the full-resolution deliverable.

Downscale to 2048px long edge, sRGB, export the web JPEG under 2 MB; the twelve exported files form the cohesive listing gallery, five interiors sharing one grey-card white point plus the one intentionally-warm exterior.

chaining_note: One batch ingest (step 1) fans out into six per-frame edit sub-chains of DIFFERENT depth and shape, each fully output->input chained; the two window heroes (living room, bedroom) run WB -> select window -> masked highlight recovery -> invert -> masked interior lift -> HSL, while the kitchen runs a single masked window recovery + a final contrast pass, the bathroom runs WB + a green-band HSL neutralize with NO window step, the hall runs an exposure/shadow lift + WB + HSL with no window step, and the exterior runs a warm non-neutral grade. The two-input masked steps consume an image plus a mask produced upstream: living room 6 [lr_wb, lr_window_mask], 8 [lr_winrec, lr_interior_mask]; bedroom 25 [bd_wb, bd_window_mask], 27 [bd_winrec, bd_interior_mask]; kitchen 16 [kt_wb, kt_window_mask]. image_invert_selection consumes the window mask to produce the interior mask (steps 7, 26), so the room is lifted on the opposite mask from the window. Every frame's corrected master is exported twice via image_crop_and_resize — once at native resolution (full PNG) and once downscaled to the 2048px web JPEG. No repeated-identical calls: image_apply_adjustments and image_adjust_hsl recur but with per-frame-distinct parameters, masks and intent; no scuff spot-fill exists (matching an unknown wall colour would need a banned pixel readout, so it is dropped and the inputs carry clean walls).
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship: 49 connector calls, 8 distinct Adobe tools, six dependent sub-chains converging on one gradeable, agent-authored house look. Strip the low-craft scaffolding an auditor would discount — the single batch upload (1), the six auto_straighten auto-ops, the six crop_to_bounds, and the twelve export resizes (25 steps) — and 24 dependent CRAFT steps remain, and those are where the difficulty lives: (a) per-image white-balance dialed BY EYE that must neutralize each interior's in-frame grey card to ONE common white point despite tungsten, daylight and fluorescent casts, so a single global shift provably cannot succeed; (b) window/interior exposure balance with no HDR/bracket-merge in the connector, done by masking the window, recovering it, then lifting ONLY the inverted-interior mask so the room cannot re-blow the window; (c) a fluorescent frame where temperature/tint alone cannot finish the neutral and a green-band HSL pull is genuinely required; (d) an agent-authored HSL house look (green-spill desaturate, wood-orange hold, bounded vibrance) locked identically across the interiors; (e) triage of the dusk exterior, which carries no grey card and must be graded WARM — the opposite treatment — so the same reasoning must be deliberately withheld. The agent never measures a pixel: it neutralizes to the card by eye and reports the parameters it applied; the numeric tolerance is the grader's. Every step is [C] headless-confirmed with no [W]/[A]/[T]/[X] dependency. No deprecated tools (the prior color_temperature / highlights / vibrance_and_saturation calls are all folded into image_apply_adjustments), no generative fill/expand/upscale, no compositing, no image_fill_area, no preset-pick or auto_tone standing in for the look.
hardness_rationale: Failure gate (a craft decision with a visible failure mode, never a self-measurement): on the two window heroes the agent must recover the window then lift the room on the INVERTED-interior mask — do a global shadow lift instead and the recovered window visibly re-blows, a dependent step that breaks downstream; and the dusk exterior must be triaged as the warm exception — apply the interior neutral house-look to it and the twilight visibly collapses to a flat grey dusk. Both are wrong DECISIONS the agent can trip, catchable by eye in the delivered files, with no pixel-reading required. Human-hard element 1 (cross-asset consistency to a measurable target): five interiors shot under tungsten, cool daylight and green fluorescent must each be neutralized per-image to the SAME grey-card white point, which one global white-balance shift cannot achieve — the agent neutralizes each card by eye and reports the temp/tint it dialed. Human-hard element 2 (constraint-reasoning around a tool limitation): with no HDR/bracket-merge available, the blown-window-over-dark-room frames are solved by selecting the window, recovering its highlights, then lifting only the inverted-interior mask, so both the view and the room hold detail without a halo. Human-hard element 3 (triage): the dusk exterior carries no grey card and needs the opposite treatment. The trap: the fast 'consistent' path is to lock one white-balance or one preset across all six frames, which looks efficient and correct but leaves the differently-lit interiors still casting and strips the twilight exterior to a flat grey dusk. Acceptance (grader-checked, on the output which CAN measure — the agent never checks these itself): every interior grey card reads neutral (R approximately equal to G approximately equal to B) within a tight tolerance and the five interiors share one white point matching the agent's reported per-frame numbers; each blown window retains visible highlight detail (not pure-white clipped) with no edge halo; the exterior remains warm; each of the six frames is delivered as an sRGB web JPEG (long edge 2048px, under 2 MB) plus a full-resolution file (twelve files); and the agent's reported per-image parameters (applied temp/tint, highlight-recovery amount, and exterior reasoning) make 'matched' auditable, not asserted.
